newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends mid-range after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends mid-range after volatile day.

text.p: IPE Brent crude ended steady after volatile trade as shortcovering sparked by Iraq drove prices up only to see profit-taking strip gains, traders said.
"Nobody wanted to go short," one floor broker. "Underneath this market the fundamentals are pretty firm."

October Brent last traded 29 cents up at $23.86 a barrel, spiking late on news that, while supportive of the deal, the U.N. security council had decided not to issue a formal statement telling Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali to implement the oil for food plan as soon as possible.
October Brent swung wildly over more than a $1 per barrel range during the day, driven up by mounting tension between Iraq and the U.S. then beaten back by a wave of profit-taking.
Prices peaked at post Gulf War highs on fears Iraq might mount an assault against Kuwait after the latter agreed to serve as an air base for an expected U.S. strike against Iraq.

A wave of profit-taking wiped $1 off the gains, but prices recovered when Iraqi state television said its air defence systems fired three missiles against U.S. aircraft patrolling the southern "no-fly zone." The Pentagon later said it had had no reports of any missile firings.

October gas oil futures closed on a firm note following the expiry of the September contract on Thursday, but Brent provided the main impetus for the rally which took prices to post-Gulf War highs, brokers said.
October gas oil closed up $3.25 at $219.75 per tonne after the September contract touched a post-Gulf War high of $226.75 before expiry.
"Brent was the real leader today, but gas oil held up well," a gas oil broker said.
The September contract expired with a modest delivery of 155,300 tonnes against outstanding positions.
